options.swap: The named cold-pressed oil of the region the dish comes from
options.ratio: 1:1. Mustard for the east and north, sesame (gingelly) for the south-east, coconut for the south-west, groundnut for the west.
options.taste_and_texture: These oils taste of something, which is the point and also the problem, mustard oil in a south Indian tempering is simply wrong. Match the oil to the dish's region, not to a general rule.
options.nutritional_rationale: Cold pressing keeps the fatty-acid profile and minor compounds that high-heat refining and deodorising strip. Comparable in calories, this is a fat-quality swap, not a fat-reduction one.

options.ratio: 1:1 for tempering and shallow frying. Poor choice for deep frying at volume on cost grounds.
options.taste_and_texture: Richer, browns faster, will burn sooner than a refined oil.
options.nutritional_rationale: Higher in saturated fat than a seed oil, better on flavour and heat stability, worse on that axis. Say both.

where_it_went: Solvent extraction and refining from the mid-20th century produced a cheap, neutral, long-shelf-life oil with a high smoke point; the regional pressed oils became specialty goods.
